utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind, you, sir, of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence. It still applies. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Witness, I'm Michael Mansfield. I represent, together with Karim Khan, Mr. Fatmir Limaj who sits behind me. I want to start by just reminding you of 2003 of the occasions when you made statements and you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor for the purposes, as it turned out, of these proceedings. Now, I just want to remind you of the dates, first of all. The first occasion was the 27th of May for which we have a record when it would appear that you spent something like two hours being interviewed. The second occasion was spread over two days in June, on the 17th and the 18th, nearly all day on the 17th, and for an hour or so on the 18th. And then finally towards the end of 2003, starting in December, but spreading into 2004, you were interviewed -- and I won't give you all the dates unless you'd like them, but it's 12 days resulting in a 45-page statement. Now have you followed so as far?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: According to the records that we have of those occasions, nowhere in any of those interviews or statements do you volunteer as part of your background that you were a heroin addict or that you had participated in drug trafficking. Now, the first point is: Do you realise that there is no record within those occasions of you mentioning that? Do you realise that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The next question is: Given what you did mention, why did you not mention that at all?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was not dealing with it at that time. And I didn't think it was important to speak about something which was bygone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, you did deal with things that were bygone in those statements and interviews, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So why not deal heroin addiction and heroin trafficking?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained to you that I didn't deem it important to talk about a personal issue such as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or is it, Witness, that you have lied about yourself on many occasions and about other people, including the person I represent, Fatmir Limaj. Now, do you agree, first of all, that you have lied about yourself and, in particular, your heroin addiction?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not lied about any of them. Either about myself when I was asked. I have told -- I have answered telling them whatever I knew about myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The point I wish to make to you straight away is that during the period of which we have a record, that is, the 27th of May through to June 2003, during that period you were still using drugs, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In that period, I suggest also you were trafficking in drugs, dealing in drugs, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, are you sure?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already stated that in some cases -- there were cases after the new year of 2003. I can't tell you for sure once, but not in June. Or in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I'll have to return to those because I'm going to suggest clearly, you are lying to this Tribunal about those matters today. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am following you very well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And so I can make it abundantly clear, I suggest you have in fact been trafficking in drugs back to a time before the war in the 1990s, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I wasn't dealing with drug trafficking during that time. I knew about it, but I didn't engage in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to make it clear also that it doesn't just involve you. It involves your family as well, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you carefully, therefore, a series of questions, some of which relate to this in 2003. February 2003. Do you remember that month at all?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know somewhere called Bond Steel?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you been there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You've never been there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been in the vicinity of that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What do you mean by "in the vicinity"?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether I have been there, and I have answered you that I passed nearby that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you been detained there at all?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you ever told anyone that you were detained there, held incommunicado?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Once when I passed by, they stopped -- detained us for a couple of hours, but no, I was not held there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who stopped you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KFOR police and army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they questioned you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything happened outside, in the street. Whatever they asked us it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But they questioned you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What did they question you about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About weapons. Mainly it was about weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why did they say they needed to ask you about weapons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was a search on their part. They searched all the cars that they stopped. They were looking for something, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were you with anyone?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was someone with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who was that? And again, if it's a member of your family or anybody that might identify you, you needn't use the name, but otherwise I don't think there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who was with me. We were returning from a coffee. I don't remember which place we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And when was this that you were stopped and questioned about weapons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in 2003, but I don't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would it be in February?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, probably in February. I think so. March or February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you engage a lawyer at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you contact a lawyer at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not about this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: About what question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember to have contacted some lawyer about that at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you contact a lawyer in February of 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, again I'm going to go carefully. Were you in 2003, leaving aside yourself, facing a serious problem with a member of your family? And I'm not going to identify in public for obvious reasons. Was there a problem in 2003 in the same month with a member of your family?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It was a serious problem, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I could say serious or how serious that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What was it to do with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to do with the arrest in a place, in a public place at night of -- and the imprisonment of that person under the allegation of heroin possession. But in fact nothing was found on him. But because of the fact that I was being surveyed and the police even once reprimanded me or warned me about that, this happened very shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This person was dealing in heroin, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This person confessed to the police that he was dealing in heroin, ten grammes of it, and he named where he got the heroin, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. I fold you that nothing was found on him, on that person or even nearby that person and that seven or eight persons were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know what was found on him then?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said nothing. Nothing. It might have been found on other persons, not on him. All of them were arrested, so because of the -- because I was considered a suspect he was too was detained. But nothing was found on him and they were maltreated by the police. But nothing was proven against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This person had to go to court, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did he receive a sentence of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Two others were released because of being under age. Whereas this person had -- was above 18 years of age and so he was imprisoned. The others were released on probation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what was he being sentenced to two years for?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not sentenced to two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What was he sentenced to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was sentenced to 16 months or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Very well. What was he sentenced for, for the 16 months?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that he was found at the wrong place in the wrong time. The suspicion was against me he a relative. He was close to me. I told you that some days ago I was contacted by two policemen and they asked -- all the questions had to do about me and not about that person. But since he was found with those friends of his, who called him on the phone, Come over they told him. And when he went there the police arrested him without finding anything on him. But because of the sentence, they took the word of the two minors who said that -- that It was not mine, it was his. What was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, sorry to interrupt. Just out of an abundance of caution I would ask if we could redact line 3 of page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you what he was found with, this person --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I suggest to you that you are telling a complete pack of lies about all of this.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This person was found and accepted possession of a bag containing cubes of hashish and nine paper deals of heroin, part of a lot of ten grammes that he had obtained. Are you saying you know nothing about any of this and it's all to do with you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you what is true. I told you that nothing was found on this person. What was found was found on the two minors and the other persons were arrested. And all of them were arrested. And it's not true that there was hashish. That is the first time for me to hear that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know someone -- I'm only going to use the first name for the moment. Do you know somebody named Alban, A-l-b-a-n?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was one of the two under aged called Alban?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that Alban was one of the minors. I don't know how they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Ramiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember. Of -- none of the arrested that I know of was called Ramiz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, you are right. Did you go to court in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The person who provided the drugs for the people arrested along with this person was called Ramiz. He wasn't arrested. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to deal with these two individuals for a moment. The Alban that you say you know, what is his second name, or does he have a nickname by which he is known?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't know his other name?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you I don't know whom you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just wondering when dealing with specific names which could identify the event and other persons if just those questions Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I myself was getting concerned here, Mr. Mansfield. If you're pursuing other names at the moment I think it might be desirable to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Witness, would you bear with me while I summarize, without giving any names, the matters that I have been asking you about concerning two particular individuals with whom I suggest you had a connection through heroin. And that that connection arose both in 2002 and in the months leading up to your arrest in July 2003. Now I want to just pause for a moment and ask you this: You have said in relation to this many times that you in fact gave up your addiction or that you stopped being addicted by January, February 2003. Do you recall you said that on many occasions?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about this carefully. Before you came to give evidence, has the -- anyone on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor questioned you carefully about your use of heroin and your addiction?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time it was when someone asked a question and on the day when I was arrested I didn't have a meeting with someone from the OTP. Four days after my arrest, after 72 hours, when I went to the police station for a statement that was the procedure followed at the time, there in the corridor I met with someone from the OTP here. And the discussion we had was in relation with this. It was a brief discussion, but it was held in the office of the inspector who I think was a German and another Albanian inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now was -- as far as you could tell, what were the questions about at that time? Because I'm asking you about whether they asked about your addiction and your use of drugs. What did they ask you about on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These sort of questions: Have you used it, when did you use it, and whatever you know in relation to this issue, it is good that you tell us here. It is good that you tell this inspector the truth. These were the words, and the discussion ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they ask you to see your medical records on this issue?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them that, but they did not do any analysis. They didn't carry out any analysis. I had the therapy with me. It was in my pocket, my personal therapy that I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, what I want to just ask you about is something you've told this Tribunal a few days ago now about this question of addiction. Now, just bear with me this is your testimony. So it's clear where it comes from, the day 51 and it's page 4325 at line 6. Just want to read you what you said: "Since that time before the new year, I don't remember very well. It might have been once or twice, small quantities. But I went to the doctor again and consulted him. So it was from before the new year up to February," and so on. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And in addition to that, you were asked the other day again about this matter, and now the day 52. And you were -- you mentioned on this occasion a psychologist and an assistant with long hair working in Pristina and you named the clinic. Do you remember doing that a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you were asked if you would help by trying to remember the name of this doctor or psychologist who advised you and who would have records about your addiction, asked if you could remember the name. Do you remember being asked that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Have you remembered the name?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I have consulted several doctors. I know that the person who I searched for for consulting purposes is in the Pristina hospital and the name of the doctor is (redacted) Another doctor who is younger than (redacted), I consulted him as well and without giving him my name or the name of the person. He didn't want to give any consulting. This is how it was. The treatment, that office said that they are very secret -- discreet. That private clinic, they said they didn't want any names, any family names and that is why I chose it. I would ask the Judges to make a redaction regarding the -- what I said about my work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The name of the doctor will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what I said about wearing the same uniform. The white uniform. Not the name, just the word "white uniform".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would it be possible to, as it were, ascertain the doctor and obtain your medical records? Would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I didn't do that, I would have been a user even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What was the question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave an answer to your question. If I didn't visit that doctor and other doctors, most probably I would have been an addict even today. It is not a job for someone who has been an addict for a short or long time to get over and done with that. Only someone who has been one can know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would mention for the record that no reference appears in the transcript to a white uniform that I have discovered. But the name of the doctor has been removed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the point of these questions, so you understand, is not about your situation now, but about your situation from January at least January 2003 through to July 2003 to ascertain whether you were using drugs in that period, whether you were no longer an addict and what the records indicate about all of this. Because the Prosecutor doesn't appear to have asked. So I'm asking you finally this: Would you have any objection to us obtaining the records relating to you in 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that there was any objection for you to obtain any kind of documents. You are free to do so. What I know is true. I have said that, I have said in the beginning I'm telling it now. I have always told the truth and although it's not something that I like to discuss, I will tell the truth. Not only in January but even before the new year in 2003 I visited those doctors, in October, in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session just Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. so I can ascertain a detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you have to pay for the private treatment?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't pay with the hospital, but I did leave some money without them asking, for the visits that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You indicated before to the Tribunal that this was expensive treatment.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How much did you pay for it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times I secured means and medicaments. None of the medicaments could be obtained in Kosova. Some of them were obtained in Croatia and most of them in Germany and Turkey. They were really expensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it will take a little time on this basis. Do you have difficulty in understanding my questions?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question was how much. I don't know how much. They were expensive. Everything was expensive. I couldn't go and get them and buy them myself. I had to use others and other channels. Someone who could bring them to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you think you have got a good memory?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do. I know that heroin makes the white cells -- decreases the number of white cells in the brain, but I still think I have a good memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Then just give us a clue as to how much money had you to spend on the treatment, and then we're going to ask where you got the money from. Do you follow? So let's have a figure for how much you spent on the treatment.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I follow you very well. On the first occasion, approximately the expenses were of the amount 700 to 800 Euros.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some cost 50 Euros, some 200, 300 Euros. Those tablets that I had to take, again, around 700 Euros. Then the travel costs for the people who obtained them for me. These are not cheap medicaments, especially not in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that you have spent at least -- at least -- 1.000 Euros on this private treatment, at least that figure?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to turn, to, I suggest, another of your major problems in 2003. You were unemployed, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2003 -- in 2003, I left my work voluntarily. I couldn't go to work and allow people to see me knowing my own state. I don't know in which month, but it was in 2003 that I stopped going to work. I think it was in March or January, February, 2003. This can be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sure that you can, so I'd like you to be very careful. When did you last work before 2003? Work in the sense of paid employment.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I got paid until 2003. I don't remember how many months in 2003. I know that I asked for an unpaid leave from work, for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where do you say you obtained at least 1.000 Euros for your treatment?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always had money, sir. And I have people who can secure me money even today. Not only 1.000 Euros.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And is the source of the money that you always have heroin trafficking?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I told you that I have real estate. And I know people who have money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you saying these people have lent you this money?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even today I can take money from them as a loan. As much as I want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are the people who lent you the money in relation to the treatment of at least over 1.000 Euros, have they been repaid ever by you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Some yes, and some no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How much are you owing? Today. How much are you owing?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small quantity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 200, 300 Euro, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How much were you owing at the beginning of 2003 before the Office of the Prosecutor began interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that amount was more than 1.000 Euros. When I left, I left behind two vehicles in a good working state. So this covered for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a few personal matters so I ask to go into private session again. I'm sorry about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again so it's clear I have been asking details about -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, so it's clear, I have been asking questions about another individual with whom you agree you did have dealings in heroin in 2002. And also dealing with where you lived and who owned the apartment. Where you lived or rather your family lived in part of 2003. Now, I want to just before the next break, still dealing with 2003. Did it come to your attention in this same period, January through to the spring of 2003, that you yourself were a suspect in relation to war crimes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During January or -- are you asking for 2003? I did not understand the question, whether it was in January or in general through 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I am sorry, I thought the question was clear, but I'll put it again. I was dealing with the same period. January were the words I used, January 2003 to the spring of 2003, March, April, May. Did you realise in that period that you yourself were a suspect in relation to war crimes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only when I received the summons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about that. When did you receive the summons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the summons two or three weeks before I reported there, meaning on the 27th. Two weeks before the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you receive it at the address in Pristina, the apartment that belonged to the Serbian? Did you receive it there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The summons arrived on that address. That wasn't a Serbian property; it was a property of an Albanian, as I said earlier. The next day the summons was brought to me in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who brought it to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone, a member of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, what did the summons say?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It said that I was to report there after a couple of days. I don't remember the date. I had to report to a place in Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. What did it say was the reason that you had to report?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The summons contained my name and last name, and the words "suspected of war crimes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did it indicate more than that about the war crimes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember year 1998 and 1999. I don't know the other part of the content. There was some other items as well. It was signed and it was sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you still have a copy of the summons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I left it in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be, Mr. Mansfield. We are asked to have a 30-minute break for technical reasons, so we will resume at 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May do I a test run because I gather there are problems elsewhere about voices being heard. So that is the statement. We'll now switch off. Okay. A further test run. Witness, I wonder if you would just assist. This is for audio security. I'm just going to ask you to say we've just had a break, so can you just say we've just had a break as the answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to say the full sentence, "We have just had a break."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just had a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you are being encouraged to have a slow trigger finger on the microphone, Mr. Mansfield. Not to have it turned on until the witness has finished the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. The finger [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have great experience with the switch here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just check, are we in public session? Yes, we are, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I was asking you before the break about a summons that was received, or that was received by your family, anyway, two to three weeks before the 27th of May and then delivered to you. It was a summons indicating that you were to be interviewed as a suspect. And I have been kindly provided with a copy of it now and indeed it does specify that you are to appear on Friday, the 23rd of May, 2003, at 9.00 to be interviewed as a suspect. And it indicated that the topics will concern personal information in general, military background, and activities of the KLA in 1998 and 1999. Now, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When you read that, did you think you had a problem in the sense that you had committed any war crimes or any crimes at all?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't clear. I thought that I might be suspected, but I believe that I would clarify that, but that I might be a suspect. And that was how it was. I didn't feel comfortable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What did you think you might be suspected of?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that someone might have provided inaccurate information about me and that I had to clarify that. I don't know whether I would be able to do that or no. I didn't know what to do. I didn't know what it all involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, just reflecting on this period. You are looking at a summons. Never mind what somebody might have said about you. Had you assaulted anyone during the war in a way that you shouldn't?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just think about it, please. Even at this stage, on your own recollection had you assaulted anyone in a way that you should not have assaulted them during the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I have ever done that. Even though it was a wartime. But I tried to stick to the front line. I tried to be as successful as possible in that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to put some specific words to you to see if they ring a bell. Did you at any time during the war, with others, beat the living daylights out of two prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you, with others, ever beat the soles of the feet of a woman during the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I threatened her. But I heard that someone had beaten her on the soles of her feet. But it was not me. Maybe I gave her some slaps. I don't remember. Maybe once. But not to hurt her in any way. Not to cause any injuries to her. But I know that she was beaten on the soles of her feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you ever use your rifle butt in any way on anyone who was detained?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. So would it be right to say that, in fact, whatever anybody else may say about you there were things you had done on your own recollection during the war that you should not have done?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was considered normal. Those were normal occurrences. Yes, I had done them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you think you should have done them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well I'd like you to answer the question. Do you think you should have done them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I should have done them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you knew that in May of 2003, that there were things that you should not have done and that you might be questioned about them, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even think of that in 2003. Even later. Because they were not important things. There are other things more important to be remembered, so I didn't pay any attention to these things. I remembered them later. I simply -- if I might, I simply thought that it was a question of some -- some murder because that act with the use of the butt of the rifle or something like that. I don't think that mattered a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived for the interview, the first thing that happened was a series of questions or discussion about why you were a suspect; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a discussion why I was there, why I was summoned, not why I was a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did anyone -- first of all, who conducted the interview or rather the questioning to begin with?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The questions were done in a small room, in the presence of an interpreter and two people from the Prosecutor's office. Before they started recording the interview, we had the -- this discussion. I can't tell you how long it took us, but we wanted to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you have told us about this earlier, on an earlier day. And you said you thought - so it's clear where it's coming from, it is day 51, page 4320, at line 22 - you indicated that you thought it was one or two hours of discussion before the interview was recorded. Now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, more or less. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now in the one or two hours, did anybody make sort of record of what was being discussed?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took notes, but I don't think it was recorded. At least nobody told me that it was being recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did anyone say that when questioning a suspect there should in fact be an audio or video recording?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, yes. I don't remember when it was, but they told me that we have to record it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they tell you why they had not recorded the first hour or two?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I had asked the question with relation to the summons. I said what it means, why I was there and so on. And this is what we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they not tell you why they thought you were a suspect when they sent the summons? The summons being dated the 15th of May. So it wasn't long before, about a week before, they thought you were a suspect. Now did they tell you why they thought you were a suspect?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't say anything, but they mentioned the fact that it was a mistake. And it seemed to me that they read it because it was in Albanian. They asked the interpreter whether it was translated in that way, and they were sure it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In other words, there was no mistake in the translation, was there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So, again, during the one or two hours did somebody tell you why they thought you were a suspect, properly translated?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They merely told me that it's -- made a mistake. That a mistake has been made in the summons. This is what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What kind of mistake did they say it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the word "suspect" of war crimes during 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, to do that would have taken as long as I have asked you, namely, three minutes to clear up that difficulty. What took two hours?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't keep the time. I don't know exactly. I said one or two times, I know that it was more than two or three minutes. It might have been an hour or more. But we discussed also that -- whether -- I mean, we discussed about the fact that they had to record the statement and all these things. I don't remember anything specific to have been said during that discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they mention whether anybody in particular had made allegations against you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you this on a more general basis. Since that time, have you been offered any kind of immunity from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. prosecution?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of what they did when I was in prison, something which I didn't ask them to do for me, I don't think of any other immunity that they have offered me. Then afterwards, about -- it was -- it was about my departure from Kosovo, if you mean this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. I will be precise. I don't mean that. We'll have to get to that at a later stage. I mean at any stage after May, when you were first interviewed, has anyone said to you, Whatever you say, you won't be prosecuted? For the war. I make it clear, anything in the war.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, this. No. They didn't say this, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask that the notes that have been referred to in relation to this session be disclosed, and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask in particular now about the beginning of the interview that took place on the -- on the 27th of May, and it may be easier at the moment if I do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Once again, just to summarise, I have been asking about questions about an interview on the 27th of May and details about your background in that interview and your whereabouts in the week before the 27th of May. Now, I want to just move on in the chronology. Do you agree that another area of interest for you in the past has been guns?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, yes. Not on regular basis, but from time to time, whenever there was an opportunity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And is it also right that your interest in guns occurred during the 1980s and 1990s?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true. From my -- age of 14 I had my personal weapon. I even know the make of that weapon. I bought it and -- by selling even my own clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were you dealing in weapons, trading in weapons, before the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What has been translated to me was "when I was dealing with this." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I will be more precise. Were you in fact involved in the illegal importation of weapons into Kosovo in the 1980s and the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1989, I secured an amount of weapons for myself, and in 1990 I sold some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to put the precise words again, even more specific. From 1990 onward, were you in involved in the illegal import of weapons into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read you to save another document. This comes from the statement that you made in December/January, that is, December 2003 and January 2004 dealing with this aspect of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So if anyone wishes to follow, it's paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What is written down is that "From 1990 onwards I was involved in illegal import of weapons to Kosovo, together with my good friend." And then you mention Alushani. And then you indicate where the arms came from: Croatia, Serbia, Albania. And that you only soldier weapons to persons that you trusted. Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very true. But even here it is said that it is in 1989. After 1989. Before that I didn't I didn't know the person you mentioned. This is the year that I meant, in the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just to remind you. It's still on the screen the specific question, precise words: "From 1990s onward from you involved in the illegal import ever weapons into Kosovo?" And you said "No." Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, import means when you bring in a great amount. It has never been a great amount that I imported. People bought weapons and those that I trusted, I sold weapons to them, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I suggest to you: For a moment you thought you could lie, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is what I said before. The word "import" came in use several times, and as import, I -- what I understand is when I go there myself and take it myself and procure it myself, bring it home myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Before the war, you were arrested on a large number of occasions, weren't you? Detained on a large number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was detained once and they kept me in for two days and I was arrested once. It's not many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm not going to mention his name in public, but there was a particular police officer who you knew in that time quite well. I'll put the context because he practiced and went hunting on a piece of land you know about. Do you know who I mean?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many people that I knew. I can [microphone not activated] I can't thing of who it can be, but maybe it's better if you are concrete who you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you have already indicated to the Tribunal that you were arrested. You thought it was 1994, and then sentenced to three months imprisonment in 1995 for a weapon found in your car. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know if it was 1994, but I think 1995 is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about this when - in other words, the background to this - in the interview in May 2003, were you not?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. For the moment, I don't remember. But it could be yes, there were many questions, have you been convicted, when were you convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And there were questions and answers in particular about this conviction, were there not?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were any, I believe these questions were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And for these purposes, I'm just checking that there is nothing --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will be careful. I think it can all be done in public session. It's on the fourth page of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you have the Albanian still in front of you, please?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And it's on the fourth page of yours where there is a question about this. I'm starting with the question: "Were you ever arrested ever by the Serb police." It's a third of the way down on both your copy, the Albanian and ours. Do you have that? The question was: "Q. Were you ever arrested by Serb police?" "A. Yes." Have you got that passage?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I haven't found it, but I know it is yes, that I have been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- the question, of course, as we'll come to, what you say about this on different occasions. It's a third of the way down. I'd like to you find the question so you can follow it in the Albania and we can follow it in the English. So it's as I say, a third of the way down. It's fifth answer by you on page 4. So if you count down 5.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm just going to read it through with you and I'll stop when I get -- just this is the context. You say "Yes." "Q. Was this -- any of these times for a longer time arrests?" "A. We were subject to constant searches and harassments from 1981 on. So all of us except for my mother had the opportunity to be locked up at some point. "Q. Okay. Were you arrested from your home and taken to a detention or -- "A. So they would -- they would come and search into our house and then pick one of us, take to prison one sister one time and then one of my brothers and then me and so on. "Q. Okay. What's the longest period you were arrested for? "A. Well, the longest period, the longest term was in 1996 about two months."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So I'm slowing. "And 22 days. So I was sentenced to a longer term. But I bought off my sentence. I'm going to pause there for a moment. What did you mean you "bought off" your sentence?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer to the lawyer. After I received a three-month imprisonment I paid the lawyer, he made an application with the higher court and then the sentence was lowered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So how much did you serve in the end?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So let's just go on. So you actually -- going back to the question. Actually, you got the sentence: "Mm-hm. I was of course -- I was acquainted in trial because I was given a sentence of three months, because I -- I bought off my sentence. I was supposed to get a longer sentence then." What was the sentence for? Do you see that question? Then you have got an answer: "A. Mm-hm. They would conduct searches, mostly for illegal arms possession or for illegal propaganda material. "Q. Okay. And this was -- did they find a weapon or something and this was the reason for?" Your answer was: "A. No, never." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't true, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to read the paragraph above. Yes, this is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it is. But it wasn't true what you were saying at that stage in this early interview in May of 2003, was it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the question was and what time it referred to. Here it says, No. The truth is that they found on one occasion a rifle, hunting rifle, from that period, meaning from 1981 and onwards. And the revolver later on. And I think that this should be somewhere in the statement although here it is, No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, there is in fact in this interview no indication that they have found a weapon. In other words, you are, I suggest, pretending to the interviewer at that point that in fact they hadn't found a weapon and you go on and talk about a hunting rifle. You weren't arrested for a hunting rifle, were you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My brother was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you this: At the time that you were giving these answers in May of 2003, at that very time, you still possessed weapons illegally, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The period of this interview, which was May the 27th. Even then you possessed illegal weapons, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I have said that. As I said in the beginning, I've always loved weapons. I don't know how I have said this. I even love weapons today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. And all I'm saying that is in May of 2003 you loved weapons such that you illegally possessed weapons in May 2003, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, maybe even today I am in a position of illegal possession of weapons. I do love weapons, and -- whether I have a document or not for its possession. This is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to ask where you are today other than in The Hague, obviously. Do you at this moment whilst giving evidence to this Tribunal, wherever you are in the world, do you illegally possess weapons now?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We are not speaking of today or here because I have passed a screening. But I was referring to the post-war period. I do love weapons and this might only be suggestions. Someone might suggest that I have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm looking at what you actually said moments ago. You said: "Sir" -- you can read it on the screen. Well, sorry, you can't read it on the screen -- "Sir, maybe even today I am in a position of illegal possession of weapons." That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is misinterpreted and this what you can verify. Today means the time now, not the -- this moment, but the time now the time after the war, these years. And I did not say that I have a weapon, but I said that even today I might have a weapon. And what someone is suggesting is not important and does not verify the fact whether I have a weapon or not. I do love weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's a simple question: Do you today possess a weapon?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can verify this. I didn't refer to today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now I'm going to -- again dealing with this incident before the war, I'm going to ask you -- and I'll do it in public to begin with, but I may have to go into private session. Have you ever spoken to a journalist about this arrest before the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you be more concrete? I never spoke to a journalist. But you're saying before the war, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. It's been published since the war, but it was a conversation - and I will be more precise - with an author who is a woman. Now, does that help you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour it may be sensible to go into private session so I can be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just once again indicate that in private session, I have asked you about a book in the form of a report published in 2003 which appears to mention you and a conversation with you, and you have denied that any such conversation took place.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It is true that such a conversation did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to pass from that. We were dealing with you and weapons before the war. Since the war, in other words, from 1999/2000 onwards, did you still possess weapons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only a few in Kosovo who didn't possess a weapon after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, that isn't the question. The question is: Did you.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A trophy weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And what trophy weapons did you possess after the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A weapon that is no longer used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, kindly describe it.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A hunting rifle produced in 1910, out of use, handmade. It was unique. And then a pistol not in use, damaged, but because of the person who possessed that before me, that's why it was in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, which weapon was possessed by someone before you and that's why it was in your possession?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Which weapon?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second weapon that I mentioned, the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And the hunting rifle, is that -- has that always been yours?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was my possession but it wasn't always mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I ask you carefully: Are you quite sure that the hunting rifle belonged to your uncle?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And did you still possess these weapons in 2003?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about 2003. I did have these weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where did you keep them?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of use. I kept the pistol out of reach of everybody. And as for the hunting rifle, I kept it inside, hanging on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Were the premises that these weapons were kept in Pristina or in the village?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village and in Pristina. The roughly, the hunting roughly, in Pristina as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So just to be clear: Both weapons were kept not only in Pristina but also in the village when you moved there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't carry these weapons with me. These were not weapons that could be used. But I said that one of these weapons I kept in Pristina as well. And later on, after some time I kept both of the weapons in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And just before the next break with His Honour's permission. These weren't trophy weapons; they were in use, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said these were not weapons that were in use. If they were worked on and if some parts were added to them they could have been operational, but for that moment they were not in use. Any craftsman can work on a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you that you're lying about that as well, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is again your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In this case -- I'm not suggesting that the others were my opinion. In this case it is certainly not my opinion. These weapons have been examined, haven't they?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can even read the expertise about these weapons and it shows that clearly there has been work done with them, that a part has been added and that one of the weapons after several tries fired. And the other as well, after some parts were added it fired too. At that time they were not in use and you could not just put in a bullet and use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you have life ammunition to go with these weapons?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The hunting rifle did not have ammunition. I don't remember. As for the other, in my house it was found. I had different sorts of ammunition. I had ammunition from 7 millimetre to 11 lying in my cupboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you have live ammunition that would fit the pistol?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire ammunition that was taken from my place was useable. From 645, 662, 9 millimetres and 12.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Is the answer that you did have ammunition, live, that would fit the pistol?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out from that live ammunition there was ammunition for that pistol that I had as well. And the entire ammunition was live ammunition. I told you that I had it as a collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a suitable moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just before the break we were dealing with weapons you agree you had in your possession, and I just want it make it clear to you that what you have said about them and their use, once again I suggest to you, particularly in relation to the pistol, is lies. The pistol was in proper working order with ammunition that could be fired from it, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true. It would have been better if you -- if you got that document I received from the expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: As it happens I do have that document. I think it's the same one. It is an expertise document or expertise report about the pistol and the shotgun.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And so it's clear, for those who have it, the reference for this it's 00079781. And it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did the report that you had contain photographs? Is that the same one? Photographs of the weapons and the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you just bear with me. There are two reports. One deals with weapons, and the other deals with drugs. But at the moment I'm concentrating on weapons in fact found in July when you were arrested. You do appreciate that? Sorry, there may be a misunderstanding. I want to know that you do appreciate what I'm talking about, namely reports on weapons found in your possession in July 2003. Do you appreciate that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you bear with me because I don't think there's an Albanian Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. version, or at least if there is I don't have it. Would you bear with me while I read to you - it's very short - the expert's conclusion concerning the pistol, which he calls item number 2 which is a Czechoslovakian pistol. He says, and this is dated the 28th of July, 2003, shortly after your arrest: "I conducted test firing by the submitted pistol with four 7.65 by 7 millimetre calibre cartridges of item number 4. It fires semi-automatic. According to the results of test firing, all of the parts of the submitted weapon of item number 2" - that's the pistol - "are functioning properly and no obstacles were observed about operating the pistol during the tests." I pause there. The expert does not suggest that they had to do anything to make it work. Do you understand this report?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But I didn't receive this report. I received another report. It had another content.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you saying that the other report said something different?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did know about that -- your report. But the one that I received said that the hunting gun -- after they put the bullet inside, they managed to fire -- they managed it to fire after four times. And in the case of the pistol, they put a magazine. After that they could fire with it. And this differs from what you told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, if there is a different report concerning this pistol, relating to 2003 in July what was found, then obviously I would be grateful to see if. But so far as we know there is no other report on this pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The Prosecution is not possession of any other report. This is the only report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I received in the prison from the court and what I was informed about, it said that, as I said, that the hunting gun, you couldn't fire it upon the first try. After several tries it could -- it could ignite the cartridge. In the case of the pistol, the attached a magazine and then it fired the entire cartridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'll come to the hunting rifle in a moment. The pistol, it is not suggested in the report, had to have anything done or added to it. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following you very well. I know how -- in what state they were, the weapons were. The pistol, in that case. It didn't have a magazine. And if doesn't have a magazine or a cartridge it's not a weapon. You can't call it a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: See, I'm going to suggest once again: Even in this detail on this matter, you are lying about this pistol, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling the truth, and I believe that the documents are valid. If they are no longer valid, you -- I don't know. You can find copies of the ones that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you have a licence for this weapon, the pistol?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't. And I don't deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a licence. The KFOR troops conducted a search. They saw both weapons, but they didn't take them away. I told them that they are old weapons. One of them didn't have munitions since 30 years. You couldn't find that brand of munitions for that weapon. And they didn't take them away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So far as the shotgun is concern the I will just read you what the report says on that. Again, the 28th of July 2003, it's called item number 1. "A 16-bore handmade shotgun bearing a number," which is then cited. "I tested the shotgun with two of the 16-bore shotgun cartridges and observed that all parts of it were functioning properly but ignition of the primer mix occurred just at the second strike of the hammer. It means that firing pin has been fixed in not sufficient way but not a significant obstacle to declare this shotgun as unserviceable." Now do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I already told you that I don't believe it. Maybe they have used the power the white powder that can be found. There is a difference between the white and the black powder in the ignition. One has another power from the other. You can't find in the market any black powder, for 30 years now. And if you put that other powder, the weapon can explode. The barrel cannot withstand the power of the -- of that powder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a little about what else was found on July the 13th, 2003. A grenade was found and you have always denied that you knew anything about that.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I deny it even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you know where it was found?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the ceiling of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How could it have got into the ceiling of your house?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If I knew -- I knew that it was a model M52. The fact that it was 40 years old, I knew that it is dangerous to hold, to keep such weapons. If I knew of the existence of such a weapon I wouldn't have been sleeping under it with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you more particularly about the drugs that were found in -- in July. You do agree that drugs were found in July, do you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Never mind what you were told. Do you agree that you did have drugs in July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I agree that they found drugs. I didn't possess drugs but they found them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Oh, you didn't possess them. Who did then?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the experts came, they took to the expertise a large amount [as interpreted]. When they came initially I denied to them that there is nothing in connection with the drugs. But when they showed me the amount, the quantity, I was really surprised and I told them that I didn't know about the existence. Had I known, I wouldn't have been sitting at ease, knowing that it was there. It would be an absurdity to tell the police that I didn't know about that. Maybe somebody has forgotten it, maybe -- I don't know. But it was not mine. This is what I know. Maybe I had it for a long time and I didn't know it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Come along, Witness. I think you can do a little better than that. First they belonged to somebody else; you don't know how long they have been there. I'm going to ask you very carefully because I'm going to suggest once again that you are prepared to lie hard to save yourself and you will lie about other people. Now, please, let's go through this. First of all -- have you seen the expert's report on this?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Exhibit number 1, that's how it reads in the report - you don't have to see it because we can do to quite quickly - was a polyethylene bag with a slit containing I think what is commonly called a Kinder egg or a box, as it's described, of a chocolate egg in red and yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And so that it's clear, should anybody wish a reference for this it's 00079783. It's a different expert, needless to say, from the last one and the copy I have has a date which is the 22nd of August when these matters were reported on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, first of all, was there a box or some container with a Kinder egg. Do you know what a Kinder egg is, first of all?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was there a Kinder egg at your house on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I don't know. I didn't know about that. I didn't see it. I have said that maybe it was. As I was told. I am not denying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where was it at the house?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't tell me where they found it. When they took away the weapons they took photos of them. But in this case they didn't show me any pictures. I asked but they didn't tell me. They didn't take this. They took a large amount. And in the records, in the report, it was said that it was one-third of a gramme.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, please listen carefully. I'm going to suggest to you that what was found on the 13th of July was all of the materials sufficient for dealing in heroin, in packets mixed with other powder so that the amount would be disguised. One packet had the heroin; some of the others didn't. Now do you understand the suggestion?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand but that is not true. What there was, there was. But about the others I explained you, I didn't know about it because it was not myself who brought it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Who brought it there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some other person of my family who doesn't live there. It is -- I was told that it is a fertiliser for the flowers. It was 20-gramme bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We really are getting into the realms of fantasy, aren't we, Witness? A member of your family might have brought it there and told you it was fertiliser? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name means. Maybe you don't understand me. Somebody from my family who doesn't live with me, he brought it for us because my wife asked for it. The expertise report said that what it writes in English it is what the report says. Not narcotics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: We'll come to what the report says in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session just for an identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Just to recapitulate, I have been asking you about who brought the fertiliser, as you were told, and you have indicated a member of your family. If you understood it to be fertiliser, how does the fertiliser end up inside a chocolate egg?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it was not found where you are saying. It was taken from my home. It was packaged in another -- with another paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was found in a cupboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It was found in cupboard. What was found in a cupboard?
