utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This what that fertiliser that I'm talking about was found either in the cupboard or somewhere else in my home. Not as you are saying, that Kinder chocolate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where was the Kinder chocolate found?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I said even earlier I don't know when it was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When the Kinder egg was examined it contained heroin. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was told. This is what I was told. The expertise verified that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: How did the egg containing the heroin end up at your premises?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am repeating it: I don't know. I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So are you saying it's a complete coincidence in July that a person addicted to heroin and has used heroin even in 2003 just happens to have some on his premises? That's a coincidence, is it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not saying that this is a coincidence. I am saying at that time I didn't have -- at least I didn't know of its existence, how it came. How it happened to be there I explained. It was in my property and then it is supposed to be mine, I have admitted that. But I didn't know of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Inside the Kinder egg, there wasn't just heroin, was there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the details. I was told that it contained only heroin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The experts' report indicates, and I'd like you to listen carefully in view of what else was found, that the heroin content was in fact mixed with paracetamol and caffeine. Now, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I told you they didn't allow me to see it. What I saw, I tried to explain, telling them that they don't need to conduct any expertise. But still took this to the expertise. But what you are saying, I didn't see. They didn't allow me to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I just want to pass on to the second exhibit which was a polyethylene bag. I think may be what you say was found in the cupboard, brought by somebody in your family. A polyethylene bag with a slit in wrapped paper, possibly a magazine, with a brown powdered substance. Is that the bag that has come from somewhere abroad?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken in my home. It was not a white powder; it was a brown powder, dark-brown powder. I saw it also in the police, and I told them, This is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Well, it was a brown substance, powdered substance. And do you know what the brown powdered substance was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what I know it to be. I think three or five minutes ago I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you saying you thought was fertiliser?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I thought -- think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's complete nonsense, isn't it? There was no fertiliser found. What was found in this exhibit, less heroin, was paracetamol and caffeine. Once again, the same mixture that was in the Kinder egg, only this time without the heroin. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you are telling me this. At the police station and even the court report said that the other contents is nothing much to speak of. I don't know what the composition of the fertiliser for flowers might be. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. They didn't explain to me. They only thing they told me was that I was not charged with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I don't think that fertiliser normally has paracetamol and caffeine in it. You do know that much, don't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is another thing what I or you may know or may understand. It's another thing what the experts say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Are you still maintaining, without naming who it was, that a member of your family brought this stuff from abroad that contained paracetamol and caffeine?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that they brought this paracetamol and caffeine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, but you see, you have admitted that this is yours, and when I asked a moment ago, you said I already told you what it is, I thought it was fertiliser. Now, we know that it isn't fertiliser so kindly tell us whether you are still maintaining, I suggest as another lie, that this was all brought from abroad by a member of your family.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, this is what I think and what I think now. I don't know its contents. Even if contain paracetamol or caffeine, this is not anything surprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Final question on this part of it: If you thought it was fertiliser, why were you keeping it in a wardrobe?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't keep it there. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Where do you say you kept it then?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't keep it. My wife asked for it and she used it for the flowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did your wife keep it in a wardrobe?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they found it. They found it somewhere in the house. It was in a bag wrapped up, as I saw it when the police showed to me. About the contents I learned later. They told me it's nothing important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now finally in the search two more exhibits were found, a plastic box with two CDs and a plastic box with one CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The reference for this is 00078794.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the first time to hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think that this misstates the evidence. The -- what counsel is relying on is not items that were found during the search but items that were tested and it's not clear that those are the two -- those two things are the same thing. So it's a small point but it could be an important point, to be precise, on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just clarify. Does Mr. Whiting mean it's CDs or does he mean something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to -- I mean it may have been a matter of confusion earlier, I don't know. But I was referring to the question that was put right before I stood up which was: "Finally in the search two more exhibits were found." And it was that that I seeking to clarify, that it's not -- the document that counsel is relying on is not a document which lists all of the exhibits that were -- everything that was found during the search or at least it doesn't purport to. What it is, is a list of those items that were tested from the search. And those could be two different things. And it's may be important to be precise on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm happy to be precise. We understood a file from Kosovo was on its way. There is a great deal more in relation to this that we don't have. For example, the obvious thing would the officer who did the searching and what he found and where would have been greatly helpful, but we don't have it. I'm doing it from a list which appears under the title of an arrest and the place of the arrest, a substance suspected to be heroin was found. And then there's the title "Exhibits." 1 and 2 I have dealt with. And then 3 and 4 do not suggest it wasn't found there but I will go carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The reason I ask you about these two exhibits wherever found, the implication is at your address, is that these two exhibits - that's 3 and 4 - that on the boxes that contained the CDs there were traces of heroin. Can you help about that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This the first time I hear about this. Nobody told me about this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. If you would bear with me. At the address in the village that you were living at then, in July, did you have a CD player?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Or did you have, if not a CD player an item that would play CDs?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have anything. There were CD, there were cassettes, there were games for children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, on this basis that there were CDs and that these CDs were found at your address, how do you explain heroin or traces of heroin getting on the boxes containing these CDs if all you knew that there was fertiliser in the house, and you weren't using or trafficking in heroin?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which question to answer. It would be better if you divide your questions. In the beginning you asked about a CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'm happy to. Can you explain how traces of heroin got on to CDs, for the moment I'm assuming found at your address?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a knowledge of a CD taken for an expertise. This is the first time I hear about it. As for CDs, cassettes and similar things, there were in my house as in any other house. But this is the first time that something else was taken from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to come to now an interview that you had with the police, the regional crime squad, on or about the 13th of July, 2003, possibly on the 14th as well, and you remember you were asked about this by Mr. Whiting who prosecutes a few days ago, when it came to light. Do you know what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now before I come to it, I want to ask you this: Why do you think the police came to your house in the first place in July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go carefully. Does it have something to do with a member of your family?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you and could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry, perhaps I should summarise first. I have been asking you about the reason for the police raid on the 13th and about another member of your family and so forth. So I'll have to come back to that. Now I want to return to what you told and the record of what you told the regional crime squad officers in an interview around about the 1th of July. May I just check before I do that Your Honours a copy of this in English from yesterday, or the day before, sorry, earlier. And could an Albanian copy, which I understand is available, be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you have a typed Albanian copy of this interview?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And we can -- it's not on the English version but it is on the Albanian. Is there a signature on each page and two on the third page and one on the fourth; in other words, every page has a signature, does it not?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And is the signature your signature?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, would you follow in the Albanian. I'm afraid I do want to go through this with you.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Starting at the beginning at least the beginning of the record it says: "On the 13th of July" -- and please be assured I will leave out any detail that might lead to identification. "On the 13th of July, 2003, the police from" somewhere "found a pistol, a hunting rifle ammunition and a hand-grenade in your house," and mentions the village. "They also found a small amount of heroin." It goes on: "Today," so it may be -- it's not the 13th, but it may be -- "Today police found evidence" in your house "in two different locations. The whole amount is about ten grammes of the substances suspected to be narcotics. According to the test kit the substance is suspected to be heroin." What can you tell us about this? Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your answer, which you have signed to is: "If I had a narcotic substance in possession in my house, I would for sure use it for myself and you would not be able to find it because I use it." You said that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What is true is that if I knew there was an amount, a small amount even, I wouldn't have been in peace. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, does the record in Albanian, please follow me, does the record in Albanian suggest that what you said - whatever you meant is another matter - that what you said in Albanian was, "If I had a narcotic substance in possession in my house I would for sure use it for myself and you not be able to find it because I use it." Does the Albanian say that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I'm reading it is that I think you're wrong [as interpreted]. This is not drugs and I'm convinced that it is not drugs. If you want, you can eat it up, all of it. This is what I said and this is what I'm reading here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Please follow. I'm going to slowly and I'm sorry to have to do it this way. You were asked a question -- I can see it in the Albanian myself, in which the word "kit" appears. We have it in bold type; yours it in brackets. Now, can you find that question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where this passage is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's on page 1. It's a third of the way down. In fact, it's the introduction on the 13th. Then there comes -- "Q. [Albanian spoken]." All right? "Today the police found," and so on. And the word "kit" appears in that question. Do you follow? It's the first question.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find this question. I read the part in the middle of the page, but I can't find where it says kit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Let's go back to the beginning. Follow from the top of the page where you will see the date and the word "May 13th, 7/03. Police" from a particular area, et cetera et cetera. Question, first question. Starts with the word "police." And what they found. And in this question, [Albanian spoken] is the word "kit" in brackets. [Albanian spoken]. Do you see that? First question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you have difficulty reading?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I said is that I couldn't find the question because here it is written "rapage" [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you that is another of your tactics to avoid facing the truth. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I told you that the word package was not mentioned here. We were -- use a word package in Albanian as well as "paket." Here it is "rap." This is what is written here, this "rap" in paper. This is how it is written here in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Witness would you kindly look at the answer. Never mind what's in the question. That was to direct your attention. The answer is -- when the officer says "What can you tell us about this." Do you see the question?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I are see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Do you see the answer very well?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to say it again. The answer is English: "If I had a narcotic substance in possession my house, I would for sure use it for myself, and you not be able to find it because I use it." Now, is that what is said in Albanian in that answer?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the next sentence, the answer is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sorry. You are evading the point. You're perfectly well able. Does the answer that I have just read out in English appear in the Albanian with you saying you use it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to the question that you asked is different and if it is down in the page, I'm trying to find it. But here it is written differently. I can read it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could you read the answer in Albanian and we'll have it translated. That is, the first answer to the question: "What can you tell us about this?" Please read it in Albanian and we'll have it translated.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you read it in Albanian I don't need a translation. We have -- I think that you are wrong. This is my answer. This is not narcotics and I'm sure it is not. If you wish, I may eat it all. This is what I have relied to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Would you kindly read out in Albania and then we'll have it translated the first answer with the word [Albanian spoken], which I understand may mean answer, starting [Albanian spoken]. Would you read that answer, please, in Albanian and we'll have it translated.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand which answer you want me to read in Albanian. If you mean the answer in the middle of the page. Because the first question was this package or this amount wrapped in paper, this amount of powder. What do you think it is. My answer comes after that. If you mean that, I read it out to you. If you mean somewhere else, please help me to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, Witness I'm going to keep on because I suggest this is very typical of your behaviour. Now, the first answer in this interview -- all right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You found it. It can't have taken you since minutes to find it, can it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, first you told me to look for it in the middle of the page. If you want me to become everything nervous, okay. Then you have your way. You told me to read in the middle of the page and this is what I did. There is not anything that can tell me where you want me to read. It doesn't have any number here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No. Witness, I read out of the first few words. And now you've found the answer, which begins the word [Albanian spoken], would you kindly read it out loud there Albanian and we'll have it translated.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's wrongly written here, "kasa." It's a spelling mistake. "If I had a narcotic substance in my home I would certainly" -- again, "kasa" use, habit. It's a spelling mistake -- "use it for myself and you'd not be able to find it because I use it." When I signed it, I didn't read this. I wanted to -- I said I have used it before. But if I had read it properly, I would not have let it be in the way it is here. Because I didn't use it after the new year, I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you as with you we go through this interview you will discover that what you are telling the regional squad crime officers is not that you have used but that you are using except for the very recent past. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am very well of that. But I said to you there are two mistakes and they have nothing to do with the proper Albanian. This is what I'm putting to you. It should be "I have used it," not that "I use it." And when I signed it I didn't see this mistake. It doesn't specify here whether I use it that day or when.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. I wonder if that is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
